solutions.check: grid and clues read from the FT's printable PDF, its numbering matching the clue list; every fifteensquared answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: In southern Kentucky, a place to drink stout? Certainly not!

indicators.note: the pub is placed in the middle of the southern-plus-state abbreviation pair

parts.note: KY is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Kentucky
an inn is a pub, a place to drink

explanation.surface: Looking for somewhere in southern Kentucky to drink a pint of stout, only to be told there isn't one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stout' looks like the beer in the surface, but the definition reads it as 'fat', and 'Certainly not!' turns it into its opposite.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone thin is the very opposite of stout, so the playful definition gives a word for very thin.

clue.text: German joiner put away in first swamp

indicators.note: first tells us the word 'in' is placed at the front of the other pieces

parts.note: taken as written
und is German for 'and', a joining word or conjunction
to put away food is to eat it, so ate

explanation.surface: A German carpenter is locked up, then a swamp appears as if from nowhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'joiner' suggests a carpenter, but it is the joining word 'and' in German.
explanation.definitionFit: To swamp something is to flood or overwhelm it, a close synonym.

clue.text: Director is a genius, comprehending outer space

indicators.note: comprehending in its sense of including or taking in signals one piece going inside another

parts.note: Albert Einstein is the byword for a genius

indicators.note: outer asks for only the first and last letters of the word space

explanation.surface: A film director is praised as a genius who can grasp the nature of outer space.
explanation.walkthrough: Sergei Eisenstein was the Soviet director of Battleship Potemkin; 'is' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Sergei Eisenstein was a celebrated Soviet film director, so he is an example of a director.

clue.text: Armenians taking only seconds to check

indicators.note: taking only the seconds means keeping the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters of the word

explanation.surface: A group of Armenians takes only second helpings to keep an eye on their diet.
explanation.definitionFit: To rein something in is to check or restrain it, as a rider does a horse.

clue.text: Nasa tutors trained high fliers

indicators.note: trained, in the sense of drilled into a new form, signals the letters being rearranged

explanation.surface: NASA's instructors have trained a new group of spacemen.
explanation.definitionFit: Space travellers fly higher than anyone, so they are literally high fliers.

clue.text: Forfeiture second after sunrise

indicators.note: after tells us the abbreviation for second comes behind the risen sun

parts.note: sun is SOL, and rising in a down clue reads it upwards

explanation.surface: A penalty is incurred the moment after the sun comes up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sunrise' is read as two parts: the sun (SOL) rising, upwards in this down clue, to give LOS.
explanation.definitionFit: A forfeiture is something lost or given up, a synonym of loss.

clue.text: Part for actor in Edinburgh — rising star

indicators.note: rising in a down clue means the letters are read from the bottom upwards
Part signals that only a portion of the following words is taken

explanation.surface: A theatrical role for an actor at the Edinburgh festival, played by a rising star.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Part' means a stretch of 'actor in Edinburgh', namely ORINED, which 'rising' reverses in this down clue; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert De Niro is a Hollywood film star, an example of a star.

clue.text: Monarch not in bed with mother of invention?

parts.note: ma is a familiar word for mother
a king is a monarch
someone not in bed is up

explanation.surface: The king is out of bed with the proverbial mother of invention, necessity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mother of invention' recalls the proverb 'necessity is the mother of invention'; here 'mother' is MA and 'of' a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Making up a story is inventing it, so the gerund means invention; the question mark flags the loose sense.

clue.text: Peculiarity of family repeatedly getting 75% less

indicators.note: repeatedly means the word for family is given twice over

parts.note: kin means family or relatives

indicators.note: 75% asks for the final three of the four letters of the word less

explanation.surface: An oddity in a family that keeps getting much smaller.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting' is a link; '75%' keeps the last three quarters of 'less'.
explanation.definitionFit: Kinkiness means quirkiness or eccentricity, a peculiarity of character.

clue.text: Last in a series for male, say, in middle of road

indicators.note: in tells us the abbreviations go inside the central letters of road
middle of asks for the central letters of the word road

parts.note: say is used to introduce an example, so EG (for example)

explanation.surface: A man standing in the middle of the road, for example.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' is the crossword signal for an example; the male sits inside the core of 'road' along with it.
explanation.definitionFit: Omega is the final letter of the Greek alphabet, so the last in a series.

clue.text: Material like mustard supplied by elderly relative

parts.note: nan is a word for grandmother, an elderly relative
'keen as mustard' is a British idiom, so like mustard means keen

explanation.surface: Fabric provided by grandma, who is as enthusiastic as can be.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keen as mustard' is a British phrase for very eager; 'supplied by' just links the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Nankeen is a yellowish cotton cloth, originally from Nanjing, so a material.

clue.text: Antarctic explorer at home with one whose barber was in Seville

definitions.text: one whose barber was in Seville

parts.note: James Clark Ross explored Antarctica; the Ross Sea is named after him
in means at home
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An explorer at home with someone whose hairdresser worked in Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: Rossini composed the opera The Barber of Seville, so the barber was his creation.

clue.text: Insufficient time for agreement

indicators.note: Insufficient means falling short, so the word for time loses its end

parts.note: a year is a period of time

explanation.surface: There isn't enough time to reach a deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Insufficient' cuts the last letter off YEAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Yea is an old word for yes, an expression of agreement.

clue.text: Stay with fool

definitions.meaning: to go along with someone, accompanying them
to deceive someone by keeping them hoping

explanation.surface: Remain in the company of an idiot.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both to tag along with someone and to deceive them over time.

clue.text: Who will get nice priest in trouble?

definitions.note: the definition is a clause standing for the people who will receive, a plural noun

indicators.note: in trouble suggests things in disorder, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Who is going to get the kindly clergyman into difficulties?
explanation.definitionFit: Those who will get something are the people who receive it.

clue.text: Youngster getting to the top must accept handout

indicators.note: must accept means the climbing word takes the handout inside it

parts.note: an ascent is a climb, getting to the top
the dole is a state benefit, a handout

explanation.surface: A young person who wants to get on in life has to take state benefit.
explanation.walkthrough: The DOLE is the British word for unemployment benefit.
explanation.definitionFit: A teenager is a youngster in the stage between childhood and adulthood.

clue.text: Kid influenced by sound

indicators.note: by sound means the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: swayed means influenced

explanation.surface: A child easily led by noise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kid' looks like a child, but it is the leather.
explanation.definitionFit: Kid is soft goatskin leather, and the napped kind is a type of leather like kid.

clue.text: Extremely sorry about a further tree

indicators.note: Extremely points to the extremes, the first and last letters of sorry

parts.note: CA is short for circa, Latin for about
more means further or additional

explanation.surface: Very apologetic about yet another tree.
explanation.definitionFit: The sycamore is a large maple tree common in Britain.

clue.text: Band heard in vineyard

indicators.note: heard tells us the word sounds like the one we need

parts.note: a crew is a band or gang of people

explanation.surface: A music group was heard performing at a winery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Band' suggests musicians, but it is a crew of people.
explanation.definitionFit: A cru is a French term for a vineyard or its growth of wine, as in grand cru.

clue.text: Deck hands given work by job-centre

indicators.note: centre asks for the middle letter of the word job

parts.note: R and L stand for right and left, the two hands
op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: Sailors are sent off to work by the employment office.
explanation.walkthrough: A job centre is a British state employment office. 'hands' looks like crew, but gives R and L.
explanation.definitionFit: The orlop is the lowest deck of a sailing ship.

clue.text: Protracted court case demonstrating one's particular talent

definitions.meaning: a strong point, from card games where a holding of many cards in one suit is a strength

explanation.surface: A lengthy legal action shows off what you're best at.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally a long lawsuit; idiomatically, from cards, a person's strong point.

clue.text: Ignore a pedant's revision, amend text thus

parts.note: to cut someone is to ignore them pointedly

indicators.note: revision means reworking, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Disregard the fussy editor's changes and fix the document this way.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of A PEDANTS gives AND PASTE.
explanation.definitionFit: Moving text on a computer is done by cutting and pasting, a way to edit text.

clue.text: Clobber animals heading north

indicators.note: heading north in a down clue means the letters read upwards

parts.note: the elk is a large deer, an animal
a cat is an animal

explanation.surface: Beat up animals going north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clobber' looks like a verb, 'hit', but is British slang for gear or kit. ELK and CAT read upwards together.
explanation.definitionFit: Clobber is British slang for kit or gear, and tackle means equipment, as in fishing tackle.

clue.text: Horse, shrew or badger

explanation.surface: Three animals line up together.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means an old horse, a scolding person, and to pester persistently.

clue.text: Search for scrag-end in Yorkshire port

indicators.note: in tells us the letter is placed inside the port's name

parts.note: Goole is an inland port in East Yorkshire

indicators.note: end asks for the last letter of the word scrag

explanation.surface: Looking for the cheap neck of mutton in a northern harbour town.
explanation.walkthrough: Scrag-end is the cheap neck cut of mutton; here 'end' just takes the last letter of 'scrag'.
explanation.definitionFit: To search for something online is to look it up with the search engine, now a common verb.

clue.text: Ghastly bra came undone

indicators.note: undone suggests something unfastened and in disarray, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A dreadful moment when the underwear came unfastened.
explanation.definitionFit: Macabre means gruesome or horrifying, a synonym of ghastly.

clue.text: South African heavyweight possibly disheartened

indicators.note: disheartened means losing the heart, the middle letter

parts.note: a heavyweight is one kind of boxer, so possibly

explanation.surface: A big South African fighter might be feeling down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disheartened' removes the central X of BOXER.
explanation.definitionFit: A Boer is an Afrikaner, a South African of Dutch descent.

clue.text: Constable taking one silly fellow round to discover great artist

indicators.note: taking means the officer holds the other pieces inside

parts.note: PC is police constable
I is the Roman numeral for one
an ass is a fool
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A policeman takes a fool round to find a famous painter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Constable' looks like the painter John Constable, but it is a police constable.
explanation.definitionFit: Pablo Picasso is among the greatest artists of the twentieth century.

clue.text: One holding chair briefly for female

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of

explanation.surface: Someone temporarily chairing a meeting in place of a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' marks the definition as a shortened word; 'holding chair' means a university chair.
explanation.definitionFit: A professor holds a university chair, and the short form is a clipped word.

clue.text: April keeps providing material for a poet

indicators.note: the words supply the stuff from which the poet's name is taken, so it sits within them

explanation.surface: April supplies the subject matter for a writer's verse.
explanation.definitionFit: Rainer Maria Rilke was an Austrian poet, so an example of a poet.

clue.text: God not bothering at first with sick bird

parts.note: Thor is the Norse god of thunder

indicators.note: at first asks for the opening letters of the words not and bothering

parts.note: ill means sick

explanation.surface: The god doesn't care that a bird is unwell.
explanation.definitionFit: The thornbill is a small Australian songbird.
